name: commands
title: Spanish Commands Practice: Tú, Usted and Ustedes Imperative Quiz
description: Practice Spanish commands: affirmative and negative tú, usted, ustedes, the eight irregular tú commands and pronoun position, with 10 sentences checked as you tap.
answer: Affirmative tú commands look like the él form of the present (habla, come, escribe), except eight irregulars: di, haz, ve, pon, sal, sé, ten, ven. Negative tú commands and all usted and ustedes commands use the present subjunctive: no hables, hable usted, coman ustedes. Pronouns attach to affirmative commands (dímelo) and go before negative ones (no me lo digas).

rules.use: Affirmative tú: él form of the present

rules.example: Di la verdad. Haz la tarea. Ven aquí.
rules.meaning: di, haz, ve, pon, sal, sé, ten, ven

rules.example: No hables. No comas. No vengas.
No me lo digas. No te sientes.

quiz.why: Affirmative tú: like the él form, cierra.
Negative tú uses the subjunctive: no uses.

quiz.after: a mi casa a las seis.
sus libros en la página diez.

quiz.why: Pronouns attach to affirmative commands, with an accent.
Negative: pronouns before the verb, indirect first, se lo.
Ser in tú command: sé, with accent.

mistakes: Using the subjunctive for affirmative tú: «hables más alto» should be «habla más alto».
Using the affirmative form in the negative: «no habla» should be «no hables».
Regularizing the eight irregulars: «dice la verdad» and «hace la cama» should be «di la verdad» and «haz la cama».
Putting pronouns after negative commands: «no dímelo» should be «no me lo digas».
Forgetting the accent when pronouns are attached: «dimelo» should be «dímelo», «sientate» should be «siéntate».

heritage: Many heritage speakers use regional command forms at home, like «dile» and «hazlo» correctly but also «no lo dices» for «no lo digas». Formal writing expects the subjunctive in all negative commands. Check written accents too: cómpralo, dímelo, siéntate.
teacher: Play a quick command game: one student gives instructions to the class with tú, then to the teacher with usted, then to two classmates with ustedes. The class acts each one out.

faq.question: What are the eight irregular tú commands?
faq.answer: Di (decir), haz (hacer), ve (ir), pon (poner), sal (salir), sé (ser), ten (tener) and ven (venir). Their negative forms are regular subjunctives: no digas, no hagas, no vayas, no pongas, no salgas, no seas, no tengas, no vengas.

faq.question: How are formal commands formed?
faq.answer: Usted and ustedes commands use the present subjunctive: hable, hablen; coma, coman; escriba, escriban. The same form works for affirmative and negative: hable usted, no hable usted.

faq.question: Where do pronouns go in commands?
faq.answer: Attached to the end of affirmative commands (dímelo, siéntense) and before the verb in negative commands (no me lo digas, no se sienten). With two pronouns, the indirect comes first, and le or les becomes se before lo or la.
